title: Admit the Record. Do Not Steal the Vault.
description: On 12 April 2026 an Alfresco REST connector is wired into ingestion. Enterprise content is governed source material. The binaries stay where they are.
body:
The wrong way to “integrate” a content platform is to copy it. You inherit the files and lose the permissions, the versions, and the place people already browse. You then have two vaults, and the new one is the one nobody will defend.

On 12 April 2026 I add an Alfresco REST connector and wire it into the VALESKA ingestion pipeline. Authenticate. List sites. Walk nodes. Search. Attach an aspect. The connector is a client: host, ticket, retry on 401. Ingestion of classified files is metadata-first. The type and aspect are VALESKA’s APQC metadata on an Alfresco node. The binaries are not treated as ours to vacuum up.

The contract

This is REST, not the CMIS path the older plans described. There is no streaming proxy in this drop, no Category Manager, no Solr configuration, and no recorded passing smoke test against live credentials. Passwords are left blank in the committed configuration. That is not a defect to hide. It is the difference between a connector you can point and a system you have already filled.

The client can list children, resolve a path, add an aspect, and search with Alfresco’s own query language. Those are ordinary ECM verbs. Using them from VALESKA does not make VALESKA the ECM. It makes the overlay able to knock on the door in a language the door already speaks.

A bridge between a mountain vault and a glass library should carry the identity of the page, not a second pile of paper. Sync state is remembered as thoughts tagged for the connector, which is a working choice and not yet a dedicated ledger. Parent placement defaults under an APQC catalog path. Each of those details is a rule someone can inspect.

What this is for

Enterprise content has provenance, structure, and permissions before it has a paragraph we can embed. The November index left files in place. This connector is that idea aimed at a real ECM. It does not make VALESKA into Alfresco. It does not make Alfresco into VALESKA. It is an admission path with a job: record what was seen, under what classification, without claiming the vault has moved.

Scripts exist to test a connection and to deploy the model. They are operators’ tools. They are not a silent copy job. If a node is created, it is created as a classified document with APQC metadata, not as a dump of the original binary into a second unmanaged tree. The overlay either respects the vault’s identity or it is just another migration with better vocabulary.

That is the same argument as the November working platform, pointed at a system other people already browse. Most users will never see VALESKA’s tables. They will see the folder they already know. The connector has to be good enough that we can find their record without asking them to move it.

The next test

The next work is a real node list against a running repository, with the aspect applied and the VALESKA record still pointing at the source. Until that is observed, this is a connector and a pipeline hook, not a migrated archive.

Historical basis: VALESKA commits 91d03c8 and 6f1469a, April 12, 2026; contemporaneous Alfresco REST client and ingestion wiring. Earlier CMIS and UI plans are not treated as delivered.

data.author: David Gargan
data.coverAlt: Documents leaving a mountain vault across a bridge of light into a glass library: enterprise content admitted by identity, without copying the vault.
